The '''Danube''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|æ|n|.|j|uː|b}} {{respell|DAN|yoob}}; see also [[#Names and etymology|other names]]) is a [[river]] in Europe, the [[List of rivers of Europe#Longest rivers|second-longest]] after the [[Volga]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Water |first=Connor Brighton 1 February 2023 in Bodies of |date=2023-02-01 |title=10 Longest Rivers In Europe |url=https://www.worldatlas.com/rivers/10-longest-rivers-in-europe.html |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=WorldAtlas |language=en-US}}</ref> It flows through Central and Southeastern Europe, from the [[Black Forest]] of Germany<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Danube River {{!}} Map, Cities, Countries, & Facts {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Danube-River |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251230221834/https://www.britannica.com/place/Danube-River |archive-date=2025-12-30 |access-date=2026-03-30 |work=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref> south through the [[Danube Delta]] in [[Romania]] into the [[Black Sea]].<ref name=":0" /> A large and historically important river, it was once a frontier of the [[Roman Empire]]. In the 21st century, it connects ten European countries, running through their territories or marking a border. Originating in Germany, the Danube flows southeast for {{convert|2850|km|mi|sp=us|abbr=on}}, passing through or bordering Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, and Ukraine.<ref>{{Cite web |last=yakubova@upenn.edu |date=2017-09-01 |title=Danube River |url=https://rees.sas.upenn.edu/about/spotlight/danube-river |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=Russian and East European Studies |language=en}}</ref> Among the many [[List of cities and towns on the river Danube|cities on the river]] are four national capitals: [[Vienna]], [[Bratislava]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Danube River in Bratislava {{!}} bratislava-city.sk |url=https://bratislava-city.sk/danube-river/ |access-date=2026-03-30 |language=cs}}</ref> [[Budapest]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Péter |first=László |date=23 March 2026 |title=Budapest |url=https://www.britannica.com/place/Budapest/People |url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Belgrade]]. Its drainage basin amounts to {{Convert|817000|km2|abbr=on}} and extends into nine more countries.

The Danube's longest headstream, the [[Breg (river)|Breg]], rises in [[Furtwangen im Schwarzwald]], while the river carries its name from its source confluence in the [[Donaueschingen Palace|palace park]] in [[Donaueschingen]] onwards. Since ancient times, the Danube has been a traditional trade route in Europe. Today, {{convert|2415|km|mi|abbr=on}} of its total length are navigable. The Danube is linked to the [[North Sea]] via the [[Rhine–Main–Danube Canal]], connecting the Danube at [[Kelheim]] with the [[Main (river)|Main]] at [[Bamberg]]. The river is also an important source of [[hydropower]] and drinking water.

The Danube river basin is home to such fish species as [[Northern pike|pike]], [[zander]], [[huchen]], [[wels catfish]], [[burbot]] and [[tench]]. It is also home to numerous diverse [[carp]] and [[sturgeon]], as well as [[salmon]] and [[trout]]. A few species of [[euryhaline]] fish, such as European [[European seabass|seabass]], [[Mullet (fish)|mullet]], and [[European eel|eel]], inhabit the Danube Delta and the lower portion of the river."}}
